title: Conditional followed by a continuation
statement: Fix a program environment, resource limits, and execution depth. Let $c$ be a condition, let $s_1,s_2,s$ be statements, and let $p$ be a proposition. In an initial state $\sigma$, suppose that if $p$ holds then executing $s_1$ followed by $s$ can finish with cost at most $T-(\mathrm{cost}(c)+1)$ in a state satisfying $Q$, and if $p$ does not hold then the same is true for $s_2$ followed by $s$. Suppose $c$ is safe in $\sigma$ and holds there exactly when $p$ holds, and that $\mathrm{cost}(c)+1\le T$. Then executing the conditional with branches $s_1,s_2$, followed by $s$, from $\sigma$ can finish with cost at most $T$ in a state satisfying $Q$.
hypotheses_covered: If $p$ holds, the sequence of the first branch and continuation has an execution of cost at most $T-(\mathrm{cost}(c)+1)$ ending in a state satisfying $Q$
If $p$ does not hold, the sequence of the second branch and continuation has an execution of cost at most $T-(\mathrm{cost}(c)+1)$ ending in a state satisfying $Q$
The condition $c$ is safe in $\sigma$ and $c$ holds in $\sigma$ if and only if $p$ holds
